We need to write JUnit 4 test cases for DataUtil. Must start with ###Test START## and end with ###Test END##. Provide comprehensive tests for all methods: load (maybe using temporary files), crossStreams, parseInputStream (harder), readToByteBuffer, readFileToByteBuffer, emptyByteBuffer, getCharsetFromContentType, validateCharset (private but indirectly via getCharset...), mimeBoundary, detectCharsetFromBom (private but can test via reflection or indirectly via getCharsetFromContentType? Actually detectCharsetFromBom is private, but we can test via parseInputStream with BOM bytes). Use reflection to invoke private methods if needed.

Focus on public static methods: load(File...), load(InputStream...), load(InputStream..., Parser...), readToByteBuffer(InputStream...), readFileToByteBuffer(File), emptyByteBuffer(), getCharsetFromContentType(String), mimeBoundary(). Also crossStreams is package-private static, can be accessed within same package test (same package org.jsoup.helper). We'll put test class in same package.

We need to test charset detection: getCharsetFromContentType with various strings (including quotes, spaces, upper/lower case, invalid charset). validateCharset indirectly via getCharsetFromContentType; also test directly via reflection maybe.

Test mimeBoundary length and characters are from allowed set.

Test readToByteBuffer reading limited size and unlimited; also test exception for negative size.

Test emptyByteBuffer returns capacity 0.

Test readFileToByteBuffer reads file contents correctly.

Test crossStreams copies data.

Test parseInputStream handling BOM: create InputStream with UTF-8 BOM followed by simple HTML; ensure charset detection sets correct charset (but parseInputStream is package-private static; we can call via reflection or use load(InputStream...). Since load uses parseInputStream.

We can call DataUtil.load(InputStream, null, "http://example.com") to let it detect charset. Provide InputStream with BOM and meta charset mismatch etc.

Simplify: test load with UTF-8 BOM and ensure document contains expected content. Use Jsoup parser to parse simple HTML.

Need Jsoup library available? The code uses org.jsoup.parser.Parser. In test environment we assume jsoup is on classpath. Use Parser.htmlParser().

Test load with charsetName specified to ensure that Validate.notEmpty works (if null then detect). Provide invalid charsetName? It will throw Validate.isTrue? Actually Validate.notEmpty throws IllegalArgumentException if empty. Not needed.

Test getCharsetFromContentType with null, with missing charset, with quotes, with unsupported charset.

Test validateCharset via reflection: call private method.

Ok produce test class DataUtilTest with @Test methods.

Edge Cases: readToByteBuffer with maxSize less than actual stream length should read only up to maxSize.

Also test readToByteBuffer throws IllegalArgumentException for negative size.

Implement using ByteArrayInputStream.

Implement readFileToByteBuffer using temporary file with known bytes.

Implement mimeBoundary: check length 32 and each char is in allowed set.

Implement crossStreams: copy from ByteArrayInputStream to ByteArrayOutputStream and compare.

Implement getCharsetFromContentType: cases.

Implement private detectCharsetFromBom via reflection: feed ByteBuffer with BOM bytes and check returned object's charset field via reflection? Actually detectCharsetFromBom returns BomCharset private class. We can invoke via reflection and get fields.

Simplify: create InputStream with UTF-8 BOM plus minimal HTML, call DataUtil.load(..., null, baseUri) and verify doc charset set to UTF-8 (doc.outputSettings().charset()).

We need to assert that doc's charset is UTF-8.

Ok.

Now produce final output.
